speaker: Teacher (mark-lifting announced)
question: What is spoken?
premises: liṅgoddhārākhyāmatha vacmaḥ — now the so-called liṅga-lifting: we speak (authorial plural).
śivaśāsanaikanirdiṣṭām — solely enjoined in the Śiva-teaching: exclusivity claimed.
inference: Charter: liṅgoddhāra, Śiva-teaching-only.

speaker: Teacher (earth-upholding)
question: What precedent was told?
premises: uktaṃ śrīmālinītantre kila pārthivadhāraṇām — told in the Mālinītantra: the earth-upholding [meditation].
uktvā yo yojito yatra sa tasmānna nivartate — having declared: who is yoked where does not turn back from it.
inference: Mālinī precedent: declared-and-yoked does not regress.

speaker: Teacher (fitness appoints)
question: Who is appointed, and when?
premises: yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva śāsanā — arisen from fitness: whose, just where, the teaching.
sa tatraiva niyoktavyo dīkṣākāle tatastvasau — he just there is to be appointed, at initiation-time; then, but, this one.
inference: Fitness appoints place and time for initiation.

speaker: Teacher (yoked and unyoked)
question: What of the yoked and unyoked?
premises: phalaṃ sarvaṃ samāsādya śive yukto 'pyavṛjyate — having attained all fruit, though yoked in Śiva, is dismissed.
ayukto 'pyūrdhvasaṃśuddhiṃ saṃprāpya bhuvaneśataḥ — though unyoked, upper purification, having attained from Bhuvaneśa.
inference: Yoked dismissed into Śiva; unyoked attain upper purity from Bhuvaneśa.

speaker: Teacher (purified attains)
question: Who attains?
premises: śuddhaḥ śivatvamāyāti dagdhasaṃsārabandhanaḥ — purified, he comes to Śiva-hood, burnt-saṃsāra-bonded.
uktvā puṃdhāraṇāṃ coktametadvaidāntikaṃ mayā — having declared man-upholding; and told — this Vedāntic — by me.
inference: Purified burner attains; man-upholding declared Vedāntic.

speaker: Teacher (Kapila precedent)
question: What precedent?
premises: kapilāya purā proktaṃ prathame paṭale — to Kapila formerly told, in the first chapter.
tathā anena kramayogena saṃprāptaḥ paramaṃ padam — so, by this sequential yoga, attained — the highest state.
inference: Kapila precedent: sequential yoga reached the highest.

speaker: Teacher (no return)
question: Does he return to beast-hood?
premises: na bhūyaḥ paśutāmeti śuddhe svātmani tiṣṭhati — not again to beast-hood goes; in the pure own self he stands.
ato hi dhvanyate 'yam śivatattvādhareṣvapi — hence, for, this meaning is hinted, even for those below the Śiva-principle.
inference: No return for the standing pure; hinted even below Śiva-principle.

speaker: Teacher (re-extractable)
question: Who may be re-lifted?
premises: tattveṣu yojitasyāsty punaruddharaṇīyatā — in the principles, of the yoked there is re-extractability.
samastaśāstrakathitavastuvaiviktyadāyinaḥ — of the giver of all-śāstra-taught thing-distinctions.
inference: The yoked remain re-extractable: distinction-giving as method.

speaker: Teacher (Śaiva distinction)
question: What distinguishes Śaiva?
premises: śivāgamasya sarvebhyo 'pyāgamebhyaḥ viśiṣṭatā — of the Śiva-āgama, distinction above all āgamas.
śivajñānena ca vinā bhūyo 'pi paśutodbhavaḥ — and without Śiva-knowledge, again even beast-arising.
inference: Śiva-āgama supreme; without its knowledge, re-beastification.

speaker: Teacher (ten-step sequence)
question: What is the sequence?
premises: kramaśca śaktisaṃpāto malahāniryiyāsutā — and the sequence: śakti-descent, impurity-loss, departure-desire.
dīkṣā bodhaḥ heyahānirupādeyalayātmatā — initiation, awakening, abandonable-loss, acceptable-dissolution-nature.
inference: Seven steps named (descent through dissolution).

speaker: Teacher (renouncing, abiding)
question: What completes it?
premises: bhogyatvapāśavatyāgaḥ patikartṛtvasaṃkṣayaḥ — enjoyable-fettered-renouncing, lord-agency-destruction.
svātmasthitiścetyevaṃ hi darśanāntarasaṃsthiteḥ — self-abiding — and thus: for one standing in another view.
inference: Renounce the enjoyed, destroy the lord-agency, abide in self — even from another view.

speaker: Teacher (extractability proclaimed)
question: For whom is extraction proclaimed?
premises: proktamuddharaṇīyatvaṃ śivaśaktīritasya hi — told is extractability of the Śiva-śakti-impelled, for.
atha vaiṣṇavabauddhāditantrāntādharavartinām — now, of those in lower systems from Vaiṣṇava and Buddhist to Tantric.
inference: Extractability proclaimed for the impelled in lower systems.

speaker: Teacher (lotus opens, mark first)
question: When mark-lifting first?
premises: yadā śivārkaraśmyoghairvikāsi hṛdayāmbujam — when by Śiva-sun-ray-floods opened is the heart-lotus.
liṅgoddhṛtistadā pūrvaṃ dīkṣākarma tataḥ param — liṅga-extracting then first, afterwards the initiation-rite.
inference: Opened lotus first, then mark-lifting, then initiation.

speaker: Teacher (even the other-marked)
question: Can the other-marked reach Śiva?
premises: prāgliṅgāntarasaṃstho 'pi dīkṣātaḥ śivatāṃ vrajet — even formerly other-marked, from initiation may he reach Śiva-hood.
tatropavāsya taṃ cānyadine sādhāramantrataḥ — there having made fast, him, and on another day, by the common mantra.
inference: Even the other-marked reach Śiva through initiation; fast first.

speaker: Teacher (proclaim his rule)
question: What is proclaimed?
premises: sthaṇḍile pūjayitveśaṃ śrāvayettasya vartanīm — on the altar, having worshipped the Lord, he should proclaim his rule.
eṣa prāgabhavalliṅgī coditastvadhunā tvayā — this one formerly was a mark-bearer, impelled, but now, by You.
inference: Proclamation: formerly marked, now impelled by You.

speaker: Teacher (grace without expiation)
question: What is asked?
premises: prasannena tadetasmai kuru samyaganugraham — by the gracious: then to him make proper favor.
svaliṅgatyāgaśaṅkotthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ ca māsya bhūt — arisen from own-mark-abandoning-doubt, expiation: and may none be his.
inference: Plea: proper favor with no expiation for mark-abandoning doubt.

speaker: Teacher (command received)
question: What follows?
premises: acirāttvanmayībhūya bhogaṃ mokṣaṃ prapadyatām — quickly become of Thee, enjoyment, liberation, let him attain.
evamastvityathājñāṃ ca gṛhītvā vratamasya tat — 'so be it' — thus the command, and having received, vow — his — that.
inference: Command received: quick divinization, enjoyment, liberation; his vow taken.

speaker: Teacher (wash and sprinkle)
question: How is he cleansed?
premises: apāsyāmbhasi nikṣipya snapayedanurūpataḥ — having discarded — in water, having placed, should bathe fittingly.
snātaṃ saṃprokṣayedarghapātrāmbhobhiranantaram — the bathed one should sprinkle with argha-vessel waters, next.
inference: Discard vow, immerse, bathe, sprinkle: the washing sequence.

speaker: Teacher (feed and blindfold)
question: What then?
premises: pañcagavyaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ tatastasmai samarpayet — the five cow-products, tooth-stick, then to him should offer.
tatastaṃ baddhanetraṃ ca praveśya praṇipātayet — then him, blindfolded, and having ushered, should make bow.
inference: Feed, then blindfold, usher, and prostrate.

speaker: Teacher (which mantras)
question: Which mantras?
premises: praṇavo mātṛkā māyā vyomavyāpī ṣaḍakṣaraḥ — praṇava, mātṛkā, māyā, all-pervading, six-syllabled.
bahurūpo 'tha netrākhyaḥ sapta sādhāraṇā amī — many-formed, then Netra-called, seven common: these ten mantras.
inference: Ten mantras named: praṇava through the seven common.

speaker: Teacher (give one mantra)
question: What is given?
premises: teṣāṃ madhyādekatamaṃ mantramasmai samarpayet — of them, from the middle, one mantra to him should bestow.
so 'pyahorātramevainaṃ japedalpabhugapyabhuk — he too, day and night, indeed it should mutter, little-eating or fasting.
inference: One middle mantra bestowed; day-and-night muttering with fasting.

speaker: Teacher (purify the vow)
question: How is the vow purified?
premises: mantramasmai samarpyātha sādhāravidhisaṃskṛte — mantra to him bestowed, then, in the rite-purified.
vahnau tarpitatanmantre vrataśuddhiṃ samācaret — fire, libated that mantra: vow-purity he should perform.
inference: Bestow, libate in fire, perform vow-purity.

speaker: Teacher (I cleanse)
question: What is spoken?
premises: pūjitenaiva mantreṇa kṛtvā nāmāsya saṃpuṭam — with the worshipped alone mantra, having made name-his enclosure.
prāyaścittaṃ śodhayāmi phaṭsvāhetyūhayogataḥ — 'expiation, I cleanse — phaṭ svāhā' — thus through ūha-practice: the spoken formula.
inference: Name-enclosed: 'I cleanse expiation — phaṭ svāhā.'

speaker: Teacher (hundreds and Vrateśvara)
question: How many, and to whom?
premises: śataṃ sahasraṃ vā hutvā punaḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ tathā — a hundred, a thousand, or, having offered, again the full oblation, likewise.
prayogādvauṣaḍantāṃ ca kṣiptvāhūya vrateśvaram — through use vauṣaḍ-ending, and having cast, having invoked Vrateśvara.
inference: Hundreds offered, full oblation, Vrateśvara invoked with vauṣaḍ.

speaker: Teacher (Tāra and permission)
question: What closes the rite?
premises: tāro vrateśvarāyeti namaścetyenamarcayet — 'Tāra, to Vrateśvara' — quoted; 'homage!' — and him should worship.
śrāvayecca tvayā nāsya kāryaṃ kiṃcicchivājñayā — and should proclaim: by you, not his to be done, anything, by Śiva's command: permission sealed.
inference: Tāra offered, permission proclaimed: nothing without Śiva's command.

speaker: Teacher (dismissal)
question: How dismissed?
premises: tato vrateśvarastarpyaḥ svāhāntena — then Vrateśvara to be libated, with svāhā-ending.
tataśca saḥ kṣamayitvā visṛjyaḥ syāttato 'gneśca visarjanam — and then he, having asked pardon, to be dismissed: should be; then of fire too, dismissal.
inference: Libate, pardon, dismiss — deity and fire both.

speaker: Teacher (third day)
question: What on the third day?
premises: tacchrāvaṇaṃ ca devāya kṣamasveti visarjanam — that proclamation, and, to the god: 'forgive' — quoted: dismissal.
tatastṛtīyadivase prāgvatsarvo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ — then, on the third day, as-before all the rite is remembered.
inference: Forgive-and-dismiss; third day repeats all as before.

speaker: Teacher (devoid of qualification)
question: What of former mark-bearers?
premises: adhivāsādikaḥ sveṣṭadīkṣākarmāvasānakaḥ — eve-rite-and-the-rest, ending in own-desired-initiation-rite.
prāgliṅgināṃ mokṣadīkṣā sādhikāravivarjitā — of the former mark-bearers, liberation-initiation is devoid of qualification.
inference: Former mark-bearers: liberation-initiation without qualification.

speaker: Teacher (converts unfit for mastership)
question: Are converts fit to be gurus?
premises: sādhakāryatāmārge na yogyāste punarbhuvaḥ — on the adept-teacher path, not fit are they, the reborn ones.
punarbhuvo 'pi jñāneddhā bhavanti gurutāspadam — even of the reborn, kindled by knowledge, they become the abode of guruhood: fit for mastership only when kindled.
inference: Reborn unfit for adept-teacher path — unless kindled into guruhood.

speaker: Teacher (Īśānaśiva's rule)
question: What did Īśānaśiva say?
premises: mokṣāyaiva na bhogāya bhogāyāpyabhyupāyataḥ — for liberation alone, not for enjoyment; for enjoyment too, through means.
ityuktavānsvapaddhatyāmīśānaśivadaiśikaḥ — thus said in his own Paddhati Īśānaśiva the teacher: converts give liberation, and enjoyment only through means.
inference: Īśānaśiva's rule: converts bestow liberation; enjoyment only by means.

speaker: Teacher (Yāmalī-knower)
question: Who performs for the low-gazing?
premises: śrīdevyā yāmalīyoktitattvasamyakpravedakaḥ — rightly proclaiming the truth of the venerable Devī's Yāmalī saying.
gurvantasyāpyadhodṛṣṭiśāyinaḥ saṃskriyāmimām — of the guru, even of one sunk in downward gaze: this rite perform.
inference: The Yāmalī-knower performs even for the downward-gazing.

speaker: Teacher (guard the secret)
question: Should the secret be told?
premises: kṛtvā rahasyaṃ kathayennānyathā — having performed, the secret one should tell, not otherwise.
kāmike kila anyatantrābhiṣikte 'pi na rahasyaṃ prakāśayet — in the Kāmika, indeed: though initiated in another tantra, one should not reveal the secret.
inference: Tell the secret only after performing; never to the merely other-initiated.

speaker: Teacher (unassured under another)
question: What if under an ignorant guru?
premises: svatantrastho 'pi gurumajñamupāśritaḥ — standing free, yet having approached an ignorant guru.
tatra paścādanāśvastatrāpi vidhimācaret — there, afterwards unassured: there too the rite he should perform.
inference: Free yet under an ignorant guru and unassured: perform the rite there too.

speaker: Teacher (lifeless mantra)
question: What of mantra from the ignorant?
premises: ajñācāryamukhāyātaṃ nirvīryaṃ mantram eṣaḥ — come through an ignorant teacher's mouth, powerless: the mantra, this one.
yat japtavānsa guruścātra nādhikāryuktadūṣaṇāt — which muttered, he as guru: and herein, not from authority-told defect.
inference: Ignorant-mouthed mantra is lifeless; the mutterer not guru here — no authority-defect imputable.

speaker: Teacher (lower-guru initiates first)
question: Who initiates first?
premises: tato 'sya śuddhiṃ prākkṛtvā tato dīkṣāṃ samācaret — then his purity first having made, then initiation he should perform.
adhodarśanasaṃsthena guruṇā dīkṣitaḥ purā — by one established in a lower view, formerly initiated: the lower guru first purifies.
inference: Lower-guru purifies first; then the true rite.

speaker: Teacher (true guru completes)
question: When does the true guru act?
premises: tīvraśaktivaśātpaścādyadā gacchetsa sadgurum — through intense śakti, afterwards, when he should approach the true guru.
tadāpyasya śiśorevaṃ śuddhiṃ kṛtvā sa sadguruḥ — then too, his, of the child, indeed, purity having made: the true guru.
inference: When intense śakti drives him to the true guru, the true guru purifies.

speaker: Teacher (unknown fitness)
question: What if fitness unknown?
premises: dīkṣādikarma nikhilaṃ kuryāduktavidhānataḥ — the whole initiation-and-the-rest rite should do as toldly enjoined.
prāpto 'pi sadgururyogyabhāvamasya na vetti cet — attained even, the true guru, fitness-state of his, knows not, if.
inference: If fitness unknown, do the whole rite as enjoined.

speaker: Teacher (test by teaching)
question: How is fitness shown?
premises: vijñānadāne tacchiṣyo yogyatāṃ darśayennijām — in knowledge-giving, that disciple should show his own fitness.
sarvathā tvabruvanneṣa bruvāṇo vā viparyayam — in every way: but non-speaking, this one; speaking, or contrary: silence or perversity fails.
inference: Fitness shown in knowledge-giving; silence or perversity disqualifies.

speaker: Teacher (no concealment-doubt)
question: Should concealment be feared?
premises: ajño vastuta eveti tattyaktvetthaṃ vidhiṃ caret — 'ignorant, in reality, just': having abandoned that, thus the rite he should perform.
na tirobhāvaśaṅkātra kartavyā buddhiśālinā — no concealment-doubt here is to be made, by the intelligent.
inference: Drop the 'ignorant really' thought; make no concealment-doubt.

speaker: Teacher (siddhānta's ten-eight)
question: Who is initiated where?
premises: adhaḥspṛktvaṃ tirobhūtirnordhvopāyavivecanam — lower-touching: concealment, not higher-means-discernment.
siddhānte dīkṣitāstantre daśāṣṭādaśabhedini — initiated in the Siddhānta tantra of ten-and-eight divisions.
inference: Lower-touching is concealment, not higher-means; ten-and-eight Siddhānta initiates.

speaker: Teacher (Trika initiates beasts)
question: Who initiates beasts into Trika?
premises: bhairavīye catuḥṣaṣṭau tānpaśūndīkṣayettrike — in the Bhairavīya sixty-four: those beasts should be initiated into Trika.
siddhavīrāvalīsāre bhairavīye kule 'pi ca — in the Siddhavīrāvalī-essence, in the Bhairavīya, in the Kula too.
inference: Even beasts into Trika: Bhairavīya sixty-four, Siddhavīrāvalī, Kula.

speaker: Teacher (lowest graced)
question: Is the lowest graced?
premises: pañcadīkṣākramopāttā dīkṣānuttarasaṃjñitā — taken up through the five-initiation-sequence, initiation called highest.
tena sarvo 'dharastho 'pi liṅgoddhṛtyānugṛhyate — hence everyone low-placed, even, by liṅga-lifting is graced.
inference: Highest initiation takes all; even the lowest graced by liṅga-lifting.

speaker: Teacher (seek many gurus)
question: Should one seek many gurus?
premises: yo 'pi hṛtsthamaheśānacodanātaḥ — whoever, from heart-dwelling-Maheśāna impulsion.
suvistṛtaṃ śāstrajñānaṃ samanvicchetso 'pi — vast scripture-knowledge should seek, he too.
yāyādbahūngurūn — should go to many gurus.
inference: Who seeks vast knowledge impelled from within: go to many gurus.

speaker: Teacher (gather initiations)
question: What of many initiations?
premises: taddīkṣāścāpi gṛhṇīyādabhiṣecanapaścimāḥ — their initiations too should take, with consecration not last.
jñānopodbalikāstā hi tattvajñānavatā kṛtāḥ — knowledge-strengthened they are, for by those knowing ones performed: many initiations strengthen knowledge.
inference: Gather many initiations; the knowing-performed strengthen knowledge.

speaker: Teacher (bee and flowers)
question: Why many teachers?
premises: uktaṃ ca śrīmate śāstre tatra tatra ca bhūyasā — and told in the venerable scripture, there and there, muchly.
āmodārthī yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpātpuṣpāntaraṃ vrajet — as the delight-seeking bee roams from flower to flower.
vijñānārthī tathā śiṣyo gurorgurvantaraṃ — so the knowledge-seeking disciple, from guru to guru.
inference: Bee from flower to flower: disciple from guru to guru for delight.

speaker: Teacher (highest among many)
question: Which guru is highest?
premises: tviti gurūṇāṃ bhūyasāṃ madhye yato vijñānamuttamam — '—' quoted: among many gurus, for whence knowledge is highest.
prāptaṃ so 'sya gururdīkṣā nātra mukhyā hi saṃvidi — attained: he, his guru; initiation here is not primary, for in consciousness.
sarvajñānanidhānaṃ tu guruṃ saṃprāpya susthitaḥ — but the all-knowledge-treasure: having reached the guru, well-established.
inference: Highest knowledge decides the guru; initiation secondary to consciousness-treasure.

speaker: Teacher (colophon)
question: What closes?
premises: tamevārādhayeddhīmāṃstattajjijñāsanonmukhaḥ — him alone may the wise worship, eager with that inquiry into that.
iti dīkṣāvidhiḥ prokto liṅgoddharaṇapaścimaḥ — thus the initiation-rule, told, liṅga-lifting-crowned: colophon.
inference: Worship him alone, inquiry-eager; the liṅga-lifting-crowned rule stands told.

speaker: Lineage seal
question: What seals the chapter?
premises: tamevārādhayeddhīmānstattajjijñāsanonmukhaḥ — him alone may the wise worship, eager with that inquiry into that: devotion with inquiry.
iti dīkṣāvidhiḥ prokto liṅgoddharaṇapaścimaḥ — thus the initiation-rule, told, liṅga-lifting-crowned: seal.
inference: Colophon: worship the inquiry-eager guru alone; the liṅga-lifting-crowned rule stands told.
